questions.question: What is the brain of the computer?
questions.explanation: CPU processes all instructions and data.

questions.question: What stores data permanently?
questions.explanation: Hard drives retain data when powered off.

questions.question: What displays visual output?
questions.explanation: Monitors display images and text visually.

questions.question: What is the main circuit board?
questions.explanation: Motherboards connect all computer components.

questions.question: What provides temporary storage?
questions.explanation: RAM stores data temporarily while running.

questions.question: What handles graphics processing?
questions.explanation: GPUs accelerate graphics and video rendering.

questions.question: What supplies power to components?
questions.explanation: PSU converts AC power to DC.

questions.question: What cools the processor?
questions.explanation: Heat sinks dissipate CPU heat effectively.

questions.question: What provides faster storage than HDD?
questions.explanation: SSDs use flash memory for speed.

questions.question: What houses all computer components?
questions.explanation: Cases protect and organize hardware components.

questions.question: Which component contains the computer's BIOS or UEFI firmware?
questions.explanation: BIOS/UEFI firmware is stored in a non-volatile ROM or flash memory chip on the motherboard.

questions.question: Which port is most commonly used to connect peripherals like keyboards and flash drives?
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is the standard interface for connecting most external peripherals.

questions.question: Which expansion card is dedicated to producing audio output?
questions.explanation: A sound card processes and outputs audio signals to speakers or headphones.

questions.question: Which small battery keeps the motherboard's real-time clock running when the PC is off?
questions.explanation: The CMOS battery (usually a CR2032 coin cell) powers the RTC chip and preserves BIOS settings.

questions.question: What does a network interface card (NIC) allow a computer to do?
questions.explanation: A NIC provides the physical connection and protocols needed to join a wired or wireless network.

questions.question: Which storage device uses a laser to read data?
questions.explanation: Optical drives read CDs, DVDs, and Blu-ray discs using a laser that detects pits and lands.

questions.question: Which memory location has the fastest access time?
questions.explanation: CPU registers sit inside the processor core and are the fastest memory in the hierarchy.

questions.question: What unit measures a power supply's output capacity?
questions.explanation: PSUs are rated in watts, indicating how much power they can deliver to components.

questions.question: What is running a CPU faster than its rated speed called?
questions.explanation: Overclocking raises the clock frequency beyond factory settings for extra performance, at the cost of more heat.

questions.question: Into which motherboard slot do RAM modules plug?
questions.explanation: Desktop RAM modules are DIMMs (Dual In-line Memory Modules) that insert into DIMM slots.

questions.question: A PC runs fine at idle but shuts down abruptly every time a demanding game starts. Which component is most likely undersized or failing?
questions.explanation: Gaming spikes CPU and GPU power draw; a PSU that cannot deliver peak wattage triggers a protective shutdown.

questions.question: Which upgrade most directly reduces stuttering when many applications run at the same time?
questions.explanation: More RAM keeps more programs resident in fast memory instead of paging to much slower storage.

questions.question: A user installs a new graphics card but gets no picture; the card's fans spin and onboard video still works. What should be checked first?
options: That the monitor cable is plugged into the GPU output, not the motherboard
questions.explanation: With a discrete GPU installed, displays must connect to the card's outputs; the motherboard ports often output nothing from it.

questions.question: Which slot on a modern motherboard is designed for a graphics card?
questions.explanation: PCIe x16 provides the sixteen high-speed lanes GPUs need; DIMM holds RAM, SATA links drives, and M.2 fits small SSDs.

questions.question: For the fastest boot and game-load times, which storage should the operating-system drive use?
questions.explanation: NVMe SSDs communicate over PCIe lanes and reach several GB/s, far outpacing any spinning drive.
